name: Vimshottari Antardasha Effects
note: Parashari astrology only; Jaimini/KP rules are not blended into this dataset. This file covers the 9x9 antardasha (sub-period) layer within each Vimshottari mahadasha. Each entry is systematically derived from (a) the two planets' core significations and (b) the classical Naisargika Maitri (natural friend/neutral/enemy) relationship table — this mirrors how classical dasha-phala technique actually derives these combinations. For Rahu and Ketu, this file adopts the most widely taught convention (friends: Saturn, Venus, Mercury; enemies: Sun, Moon, Mars; neutral: Jupiter and each other's node) as its DECIDED, fixed convention for nodal relationships. Classical texts do not universally agree here, but no alternative convention found wider or better-attested support during review, so this one is treated as settled for this dataset rather than left open. approx_duration_months is computed with the standard Vimshottari shortcut (mahadasha_years x antardasha_planet_years / 10); exact sub-period start/end dates for a real chart require the native's precise mahadasha balance at birth, which this static reference table does not calculate. This layer should always be read together with the mahadasha layer (vimshottari_mahadasha) and with each planet's own dignity and house placement in the individual chart, not in isolation.

verification_pass.method: Cross-checked the full 7-planet Naisargika Maitri (natural friend/enemy/neutral) table this entire file is generated from against multiple independent online sources, cell by cell, since all 81 entries derive from this one table plus the duration formula (already verified in vimshottari_mahadasha.json).
verification_pass.unchanged_after_verification: All 7x7 classical friend/enemy/neutral relationships confirmed exactly as used (including Jupiter's enemies being BOTH Mercury and Venus — one source consulted during this pass had an incomplete-looking table that seemed to omit Venus, but two other independent sources confirmed both Mercury and Venus as Jupiter's enemies, matching this file).

user_review_pass.method: Spot-check sampling across the file following the online-source verification pass above; the previously-flagged Rahu/Ketu nodal-relationship convention was reviewed and adopted as this dataset's fixed default (see note field) rather than left as an open question.
user_review_pass.outcome: Approved. All 81 items marked verified: true.

generated_by: Claude (Cowork) - drafted from training knowledge, cross-checked against online sources; still recommend a final pass against your primary reference text

items.title: Sun Antardasha in Sun Mahadasha
items.summary: Sun's own sub-period within its own Sun Mahadasha — a consolidating, high-point phase.
items.effects: During the Sun Mahadasha, the Sun Antardasha brings a sub-period of roughly 3.6 months in which the themes of authority, self-confidence, vitality, the father, and government or official matters come into active focus, expressed within the broader, ongoing context of authority, self-confidence, vitality, the father, and government or official matters that characterizes the overall Sun Mahadasha. This is the planet's own sub-period within its own main period (Swabhukti). Classically, this tends to consolidate and intensify the Mahadasha's core themes rather than introducing a new direction, and often marks a notable turning point or high point within the period.

items.title: Moon Antardasha in Sun Mahadasha
items.summary: Brings Moon's themes (the mind, etc.) into focus within the Sun Mahadasha (friend relationship).
items.effects: During the Sun Mahadasha, the Moon Antardasha brings a sub-period of roughly 6.0 months in which the themes of the mind, emotions, the mother, public life, and adaptability come into active focus, expressed within the broader, ongoing context of authority, self-confidence, vitality, the father, and government or official matters that characterizes the overall Sun Mahadasha. Moon is a natural friend of Sun (per classical Naisargika Maitri), so this sub-period generally supports and harmonizes with the Mahadasha's themes, tending to produce smoother, more cooperative results — provided both planets are reasonably well-placed in the individual chart.
